sentiment: Old engines wake again while quiet batteries hold the dark, and something always-on learns to wait.

stories.title: Dots: Always-on agents
stories.summary: An agent that never sleeps is really a study in waiting — listening, holding context, deciding when a moment is worth acting in. Presence without constant motion is its own discipline.

stories.title: Vermont replacing power plants with home batteries
stories.summary: A grid stitched out of ordinary homes, each holding a little charge for the night. The reserve is not in one great plant but distributed, quiet, and patient — the dark held back by many small cells.

stories.title: NASA asked several former SR-71A staffers to help secret restart
stories.summary: An aircraft long retired is coaxed back by the people who once knew its rhythms by hand. Old engines do not forget how to run — they just wait for someone who still remembers how to wake them.
